stem:
Priya is finding the volumes of four objects in her school laboratory.

Which objects should have their volumes found by water displacement in a measuring cylinder, not by a shape formula?

| object | W | X | Y | Z |
| description | iron cube of side 3 cm | piece of stone | wooden block 5 cm × 2 cm × 4 cm | broken piece of brick |
tables: {"headers":["object","W","X","Y","Z"],"rows":[["description","iron cube of side 3 cm","piece of stone","wooden block 5 cm × 2 cm × 4 cm","broken piece of brick"]],"row_labels":["description"],"caption":""}

teacher.key_rationale: Only regular shapes (cube W and cuboid Y) allow a shape formula V = l × b × h. The stone (X) and broken brick piece (Z) are irregular, so their volumes must be found by water displacement: final reading minus initial reading. Hence X and Z, option B.
